Die Dokumentation dieser Integration wird von ihrem Autor geschrieben und ist bisher nur auf Englisch verfügbar.

Brings the thermostat zones of a **Heatmiser neoHub** into Gladys, on your
local network, through the official local API of the hub (a secure WebSocket on
port 4243, authenticated by an API token of the hub). Unofficial, not
affiliated with Heatmiser. **Never tested with a real device yet**: written
from the official "neoHub API" document of IMI Heatmiser; your feedback is
welcome.

## What you get

- One device per **thermostat zone** (neoStat, neoAir): the room temperature,
  the setpoint, and the mode: **Schedule** (the zone follows its program) or
  **Standby** (frost protection: the zone holds its frost temperature).
- One device for the **hub**: the **away mode** (Home / Away). Away puts every
  thermostat in standby and turns the time clocks and neoPlugs off (PDF of
  Heatmiser): it acts on everything the hub drives.
- Time clocks, plugs and the time clock half of a combined neoAir are not
  shown in this version.

## Setup

1. In the **Heatmiser Neo** app: Settings > API Access > Tokens, create a token.
2. In Gladys, open the integration: type the **IP address** of the hub (shown in
   your router; give the hub a fixed address there) and the **token**, save.
3. Click **Test the connection** once, **from your home network**: it reads the
   certificate the hub shows and **learns** its fingerprint (shown in the
   answer and in the status). It is learnt, **not verified**: the hub makes
   its own certificate, there is no authority to check it against. Someone who
   controls your local network at that very click could have his own
   certificate learnt instead and receive the token. To verify, compare the
   fingerprint shown with the one of your hub, read from a computer of your
   network: `openssl s_client -connect \<hub address>:4243 \</dev/null 2>/dev/null
| openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256`. You may also type the
   fingerprint yourself instead of clicking. From then on, the token goes to
   that certificate only.
4. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the zones and the hub.

The token is kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, and sent only
to the hub at the address you typed, over the learnt certificate. It does not
appear in the logs, the status nor the files of the integration.

## Commands

**Standby** on a zone and **Away** on the hub need no option. Standby only
lowers the heating of its zone; away puts every thermostat in standby and
turns the time clocks and neoPlugs off. They are sent at once, before any
other command waiting (a read of the hub stuck for 1 s is cut for them),
addressed by the device number of the zone; the standbys of a scene leave
together in one command. A hub that refuses device numbers gets the zone at once
by the name its last read gave (one command per zone); one that answers
numbers without doing anything gets it by name when the stop is sent again
(about 90 s later, see below). Once the hub refused a number and then took
the name, it is sent names from then on, also after a restart; a zone whose
name holds a quote or a backslash still goes by its number. On a hub that
ignores numbers, such a zone cannot get a standby from Gladys (the status and
the badge say "not applied"): rename it in the Heatmiser Neo app. Gladys gets its answer within about
3.4 s; a stop that could not leave by then stays in line and leaves as soon as
the hub is free. A stop is done as soon as a read of the hub shows it, and a
change you make later in the app wins (never sent again). The hub refreshes
its data about every 90 s: a stop it answered is "not yet visible" until a
read sent at least 90 s after its answer; if that read does not show it, or
the hub did not answer, the stop is sent again with the next reads (by
number, and by name when the name can be sent), 3 times at most, and the
status and the badge of the zone say so. That window lasts until the first read
made 90 s or more after the answer, so up to the refresh interval when it is
longer (600 s at most). A change made in the app during that window cannot be
told from a stop not applied: it may be overwritten, 3 times at most. A newer Schedule (or Home) that left
lifts the stop: it is not sent again, not even after a restart. A Schedule (or
Home) refused before leaving (option off, pause, too late) leaves the stop to
be sent. A command asked before a standby on the same zone (before an away, on
any zone) that has not left yet is cancelled. What a stop needs all the same:
the address, the token and the learnt certificate (without them nothing can be
sent to the hub); it is refused when another hub answers at the address, and
it is not sent again by itself after the hub refused the token (a click sends
it, or a new token).

These commands are **off by default** and need the option **Allow heating
commands**:

- the **setpoint** of a zone (5 °C to the ceiling, 24 °C by default, rounded
  down to 0.5 °C, by steps of 0.5 °C);
- **Schedule** on a zone (leaves the standby);
- **Home** on the hub (leaves the away mode).

Each is decided on a fresh read of the hub (a read sent after the command
arrived; the hub, the zone at its device number and its name at the previous
read checked), addressed by the device number of the zone, sent within 2.8 s
or refused unsent, then read back; Gladys gets its answer within about 3.4 s.
As for the stops, a value the data of the hub does not show yet is "not shown
yet", and is told as not applied only by a read made 90 s or more after it
left (a follow-up read is made 95 s after). The same setpoint (or Schedule) asked of several
zones at once leaves in one command; different setpoints leave one after the
other, each within its own 2.8 s, the others refused unsent ("too late"). A
setpoint is refused:

- when the option is off, or the value is outside 5 °C to the ceiling or not a
  multiple of 0.5 °C;
- while the zone is in standby, away or on holiday, or the hub is away or on
  holiday (choose Schedule or Home first);
- for 10 minutes after a standby of the zone or an away of the hub, unless
  Schedule or Home has left since;
- when the hub is set to °F (only °C is supported), or its unit is not read
  yet (again after any change of the system of the hub);
- when the zone is offline, gone, or renamed since the previous read (try
  again); right after a restart, the name kept at the Scan and a read of the
  unit within the command are used;
- when 8 commands already wait, during a pause after failed reads, after a
  refused token, or when its turn does not come in time (nothing sent).

Schedule and Home are refused when /data cannot keep that they lift a stop
(nothing sent).

A command that may have reached the hub is never told "not sent": you get
"sent, without confirmation" and the next reads show the result. No command
goes through a switch: a "turn everything off" never reaches the heating.

## Reads and pace

The hub is read every 60 s by default (30 to 600 s; the hub refreshes its own
data about every 90 s); the button, the Discovery tab or a restart never read
it sooner than the interval. A command adds its own reads: one before it, one
right after it, then 5 s and 20 s later. After a failure the integration waits 1, 2, 5, 10
then 15 minutes. A token refused by the hub stops the automatic reads until you
type a new token or click Test the connection.

If the hub is replaced or reset, its certificate changes: nothing is sent and
the status shows the new fingerprint; type it in the configuration once you
have checked it is your hub.

## Data

`/data/heatmiser-neohub-state.json` keeps the time of the last read, the pause,
the learnt certificate fingerprints, the stop commands still to send, and,
for a refused token, an 8-bit tag (never the token).

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt Heatmiser neoHub in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Heatmiser neoHub | `section` | Nein | Brings the thermostat zones of your Heatmiser neoHub into Gladys, on your local network, through the official local API of the hub (secure WebSocket, port 4243): the temperature, the setpoint and the mode (schedule or standby) of each zone, and the away mode of the hub. Create an API token in the Heatmiser Neo app (Settings > API Access > Tokens), type it below with the address of the hub, save, then click "Test the connection" once, from your home network: it learns the fingerprint of the certificate of the hub (learnt, not verified: the guide tells how to compare it). Standby and away need no option; setpoints and the return to the schedule stay off until allowed below. Never tested with a real device yet. Unofficial, not affiliated with Heatmiser. |
| Address of the neoHub | `string` | Ja | The local IP address of your neoHub, like 192.168.1.40 (shown in your router). Port 4243 unless you add ":port". |
| API token of the hub | `secret` | Ja | Created in the Heatmiser Neo app: Settings > API Access > Tokens. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, and sent only to the hub at the address above, over its learnt certificate. |
| Certificate fingerprint (optional) | `string` | Nein | The SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate of the hub (the hub makes its own certificate). Empty: learnt on your first click of "Test the connection" (learnt, not verified: do it from your home network and compare it as the guide shows), then checked on every connection; the token never goes to another certificate. If the hub is replaced or reset, type here the fingerprint the status shows. |
| Heating commands (off by default) | `section` | Nein | Standby of a zone (frost protection) and the away mode of the hub need no option: standby only lowers the heating of its zone; away puts every thermostat in standby and turns the time clocks and neoPlugs off. Without the option below, Gladys sends nothing else. Setpoints, Schedule and Home are decided on a fresh read of the hub. No command goes through a switch: a "turn everything off" never reaches the heating. |
| Allow heating commands | `boolean` | Nein | The dashboard, the scenes and the voice assistants may change the setpoint of a zone, put a zone back on its schedule and leave the away mode. |
| Setpoint ceiling (°C) | `number` | Nein | A setpoint above this value is refused (16 to 35 °C). |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | Nein | Seconds between two reads of the hub (30 to 600). The hub refreshes its own data about every 90 s. |
| Language of the names | `select` | Nein | Used for the names of the devices, features and options added from now on. |

## So installierst du Heatmiser neoHub in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: Heatmiser neoHub erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-heatmiser-neohub:0.1.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-heatmiser-neohub](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-heatmiser-neohub).

Heatmiser neoHub benötigt Gladys `>=5.3.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

Heatmiser neoHub ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
